page: Amazon Web Services r6id.32xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 128 vCPUs and 64 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing Intel Xeon 8375C processors running at 3.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 1024.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 7600 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieved a top-tier rating in the Passmark CPU score of 87085.72 and extended instructions test of 108416.7, alongside a strong stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score of 123840.21. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 6623.09 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 135.74 GB/sec. For database operations, the server demonstrated strong capabilities with 106.91 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a strong Passmark database operations score of 29749.19.

While single-core performance benchmarks like stress-ng and Geekbench single-core fall into the average tier, the massive memory footprint and high-speed local NVMe storage offer qualitative cost efficiency for resource-dense, memory-bound workloads. The absence of a GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, though it maintains strong performance for smaller LLM inference tasks, such as prompt processing on 7B models at 194.22 tokens per second. The hardware profile is optimized for large-scale databases, in-memory caching, data analytics, and enterprise applications requiring high memory-to-vCPU ratios and fast local scratch space.
